evidence.V1: Silhouette reads instantly as anvil-on-stump from front, three-quarter and top (horn, face, waist, banded stump all distinct at 64 px).
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: big = anvil body + stump, medium = waist foot, iron bands, cream top ring, small = hardy hole and horn tip.
evidence.V3: Anvil body and waist are near-straight boxes and the horn is a plain straight cone with no downward curve or taper into the body; reads stiff rather than confidently stylised, stump is chunky and good.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on face, heel, waist foot and stump rims catch light in the studio close-ups; horn-to-body join has no blend but edges elsewhere are uniform.
evidence.V5: No z-fighting or patches; horn close-up shows a soft uneven shading crease along the cone and a visible collar where the horn penetrates the body (A16 penetration 0.032), minor.
evidence.V6: Steel grey anvil, one wood hue in values, ink iron bands, cream stump top: disciplined palette with good value contrast.
evidence.V7: 1120 tris vs medium target 2000 / ceiling 4000: well under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, steel greys + ink + cream accents, chamfer width matches kit; colourways swap only the wood hue as expected.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct for a furniture prop.

artifacts: slight shading crease along horn cone
hard collar where horn cone penetrates the body face
top_fixes: Give the horn a proper anvil profile: curve its underside up into the body and blend the join instead of a straight cone poking out
Add taper/waisting to the anvil body and waist (narrower waist, flared feet, slightly drooping heel) to break the boxy primitive look
Sink the hardy hole as a real recess with a chamfered rim rather than a flat black square
